name: Canarys Automations Limited
summary: Acquisition-led scale offers a credible opportunity, but weak legacy cash conversion, ageing receivables and remaining minority-buyout obligations prevent a clean compounder conclusion. Completed conditional annual models distinguish commercial upside from unresolved component reporting and organic-growth evidence.
identity_note: Primary sources identify legal company and listing; verify any later migration before execution.
score_note: Original-weight missing-data bounds retained. REV and R are genuine low-confidence economic inputs, not unperformed arithmetic. Supported factors retained; persistent CASH 2 caps GQS 5. G2 hold independently excludes rankings.

gates.reason: Approved allocation and unmodified opinion balanced with high remuneration, audit-trail exception and unaudited component scope; no abuse finding.
Material component cash/organic growth and acquisition cash bridge unresolved despite supported FX and capital-flow reconciliation.
Buyout pricing and future funding commitment not established; linked scenarios expose required debt/dilution rather than assume sanction.
Official full 60 day data and quote/lot verified; concentration/market-making/price variation cautions constrain execution.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Canarys is an IT-services and water-automation business undergoing acquisition and product transitions, not yet a proven SaaS compounder. Fortira drove most headline scale growth; water revenue fell sharply. Several apparent accounting discrepancies can be reconciled, including warrant cash and preference redemption, and much of the subsidiary profit difference follows disclosed currency translation. Genuine gaps remain in acquisition-adjusted cash flow, independently audited components and remaining-stake pricing. Conditional base valuation gives ₹70.61 terminal value and20.24% five-year CAGR from the dated ₹28.10 quote, but this is not a certified expected return. BQS/GQS/IAS remain NS with substantial supported factors, not blanket missing research. [S1][S2][S4][S5][S7][S90]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Canarys Automations Limited, INE0QG301017, NSE CANARYS/SM, SME at 20 October 2026; issuer confirms listing 11 October 2023. Current 58,744,893 shares agree with the NSE further-listing letter and annual report. Quote ₹28.10 is official19October close, not live. Consolidated Accounting Standards statements include wholly owned US/Singapore subsidiaries,51% Fortira and49% proportionate consolidation of the Hanuka joint venture. Group PAT is used for group CFO comparisons; parent-attributable PAT is used for EPS. March 2026 is the model opening date. Five synthetic years,15% hurdle and ₹5 lakh liquidity test. G1 conditional, G2 and G3 unresolved holds, G4 conditional. [S1][S5][S8][S90][S91]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: GOV4, MOAT4, DUR5, CAP5, CASH2, BAL5, EXEC5 and EARN5 are supported. REV is NS: acquisition scope, historical intersegment eliminations and cloud pass-through prevent a reliable comparable demand-growth basis. This is not an undisclosed acquisition haircut. CAP uses full acquisition capital and an explicit development-expensing sensitivity; CASH includes older negative years and current ageing. Persistent CASH2 caps any scoreable GQS at 5. D2/P5/L4 are supported; R remains NS because the conditional valuation depends on unresolved component cash and minority terms. No aggregate is renormalized or assigned a midpoint. [S1][S2][S3][S4][S7][S90][S96]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Technology work spans DevOps, digital transformation, cloud services and software delivery; water-resource automation involves engineering projects with a longer operating cycle. FY26 technology revenue ₹184.3458 crore and water ₹13.8002 crore are economically different. Purchases of goods/services plus other direct expenses total ₹79.7743 crore, so gross billings are not recurring software value added. Fortira adds US enterprise access and delivery capability. AURYIS, ClubAce, Scholaris and the modernization framework are product ambitions with different development/commercial stages; no verified group ARR or cohort-retention metric supports applying SaaS multiples to all sales. [S1][S7][S10][S11]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Long-standing vendor partnerships, technical knowledge and named enterprise contracts provide ordinary relationship advantages. The prospectus disclosed top-ten customers at 50.54% of FY23 revenue, and recent Calibo/LinkedIn orders broaden observed activity. Against that, cloud licences and staff-intensive implementation remain competitive and can carry pass-through economics; customer concentration and skilled-employee retention matter. Management’s 100% retention and AI-productivity claims are not audited recurring-revenue KPIs. Comparison should be with IT implementation/cloud resellers and project automation, not an unqualified pure-play AI/SaaS multiple. Competitor financial multiples are not introduced without comparable scope and cash economics. [S1][S3][S7][S10][S11] DEV Information Technology’s own service catalogue demonstrates overlapping cloud, managed-IT and enterprise-application competition. Its scale, subsidiary mix and financial valuation are not assumed equivalent. [S14]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Reported consolidated sales were ₹25.6172/51.5090/74.5194/75.0152/89.0827/198.1460 crore FY21–26. Latest growth 122.43% and FY23–26 CAGR 38.54% are acquisition-affected; pre-acquisition FY23–25 CAGR was 9.34%. Fortira AOC-1 sales ₹109.175 crore use closing FX; consolidation uses average FX. A rough ₹104.03 crore average-rate run-rate proxy is useful for scenario sizing, not a proven organic bridge. Parent services to Fortira ₹13.031 crore require elimination. FY25 segment gross sales ₹92.0827 crore include ₹3 crore intersegment elimination to group ₹89.0827. Water declined 56.07%. These scope issues are why REV remains NS rather than scoring acquisition doubling as organic growth. [S1][S2][S3][S4]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: July management backlog ₹441 crore comprises technology 206, Fortira 207 and water 28, but is not an independently reconciled executable-backlog schedule. September Calibo India ₹11.6352 crore and Calibo Inc USD 780000 are distinct twelve-month disclosures; July GNIDA Phase A ₹9.8488645 crore supports a possible water recovery. No pipeline or cloud order is converted directly to high-margin product sales. Development assets rose ₹5.4116 to11.8164 crore; the earlier FY26 modernization-framework launch target moved to FY27 in the notes. Full-capital average return proxy 18.72% and incremental 20.23% fall to about 14.64%/16.76% when development spending and assets are consistently expensed/removed. Goodwill remains in acquisition capital. Cash commercialization, not capitalization, must validate the runway. [S1][S2][S7][S10][S11][S12]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The 51% Fortira transaction, completed 15 April 2025, was disclosed as unrelated-party despite earlier business with the target. The IPO object variation was approved by shareholders on 4 December 2024; it is not characterized as unauthorized diversion. The remaining 49% is to be acquired within three years, but complete pricing terms were not found. Five executive directors received ₹5.4439 crore, 44.18% of owners’ PAT, versus ₹3.314 crore in FY25. Separate travel reimbursements are not automatically private benefits. iBOTOmate sales ₹2.4917 crore and receivables ₹2.5431 crore need commercial-terms and collection monitoring, not an inference of abuse.

The FY26 group auditor’s Other Matters section says specified foreign-subsidiary and joint-venture accounts were unaudited and furnished by management. The group opinion was not qualified on that account. The consolidated notes disclose audit-trail exceptions in certain payroll, PPE, inventory and database processes, alongside management’s assessment that internal controls were effective. These are specific disclosed scope/control limitations, not a finding of manipulation. The annual report lists income-tax and GST appeal amounts totaling ₹0.7957 crore. They are disputed exposures, not adjudicated misconduct or a prediction of loss. No subsequent final resolution was located by the review cutoff. Product-launch slippage offsets delivered acquisition and order milestones. [S1][S2][S4][S6][S8]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: Five-year FY22–26 CFO totals −₹10.1884 crore despite positive aggregate group PAT. FY26 CFO ₹6.5498 minus cash capex ₹6.5591 is approximately zero before acquisitions; capitalized development accounts for ₹6.4048 of the year’s increase. Receivables ₹80.2588 crore include ₹25.3837 crore overdue more than one year and ₹9.4287 crore beyond three years, up from ₹2.2221 crore. Classification as good is not collection. FX policy explains much of Fortira AOC-1PAT 5.3808 versus consolidated 5.1272; exact scope/translation residuals remain. Acquisition CF records goodwill 22.5505 and minority movement −.9117, but Note 5 calls the latter a noncash acquisition reserve. With initial cost 21.798, an illustrative cash identity gives adjusted CFO 4.8856 minus acquired cash if other entries hold; this is a diagnostic, not an audited restatement. Current-tax/deferred-tax/provision movements must be bridged together, not called double-tax error. FY25 cash 29.3179 versus recast 27.8058 aligns with about 1.5121 long-term-deposit reclassification and unchanged CFO. [S1][S2][S3][S4]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The dated ₹28.10 quote implies ₹165.07 crore equity and about 13.40× reported owners’ PAT of ₹12.3214 crore. This earnings-multiple cross-check is not a normalized SaaS valuation. Full exercise of 1,587,000 granted options at ₹2 gives 60,331,893 diluted shares and ₹0.3174 crore proceeds. All old warrants are converted: FY26 cash ₹4.7625 less preference redemption ₹1.56 equals ₹3.2025; neither is counted again. Models separate Fortira, other technology and water, full development cash and five-year cohort amortization, working capital, minority distributions, interest and financing. The remaining 49% is due within three years of 15 April 2025. Funding/purchase is therefore assumed at year 2 close, just ahead of April 2028, with 100% ownership from year 3; it is not deferred to the end of year 3. First two years retain assumed minority distributions. Opening current provisions ₹5.6006 crore are settled in year 1 separately from future tax and employee charges, an explicit cash-timing assumption.

Base assumptions are Fortira/other-tech growth 10%/15%, water sales ₹18/22/25/28/31 crore, EBITDA margins 8%/18%/12%, tech/water net-WC ratios 30%/110%, annual development cash ₹6 crore and minority purchase ₹22 crore. Physical capex, development amortization and full-opening plus half-year new-draw interest are deducted. At 11× exit EBIT, terminal price is ₹70.6148 and five-year CAGR 20.24%, requiring ₹21.1019 crore cumulative new borrowing and ₹27.8548 crore peak debt. Bear ₹0.0000/−100.00% and bull ₹194.0341/47.18% require ₹57.1873/15.6023 crore new borrowing respectively. Bull repays its temporary funding by the terminal year; zero terminal debt is not zero financing need. These are conditional requirements, not sanctioned headroom or expected returns.

Buyout ₹44 crore gives 18.46%; technology WC ten percentage points higher gives 17.55%; 16% interest gives 20.10%. A ₹12.75 crore debt ceiling, itself conditional on renewal of bank and related funding, forces base hypothetical equity ₹14.3685 crore at 80% of the dated quote and reduces return to 18.88%. With both the larger buyout and that ceiling, equity need is ₹36.3685 crore and return 15.67%. The no-incremental-funding case has a funding gap and no reported investor return. Two-way technology growth ±5 percentage points versus exit 9/11/13× EBIT yields 10.39%–29.95%, with complete recalculated cash/debt bridges. At 12%/15%/18% equity hurdles, the reference spread is 8.24/5.24/2.24 percentage points; conditional maximum entry values are ₹40.07/35.11/30.88. This is not an intrinsic-value guarantee. Goodwill is not added as NAV or paid again. [S1][S4][S5][S7][S90]

Opening-claim model review, 20 October 2026: ₹0.1323 crore rent-equalisation reserve and ₹0.0330 crore refundable deposit liability were omitted from the earlier terminal bridge. The revised model retains ₹0.1653 crore against terminal equity, without an immediate cash payout or second rental expense. Annual rent expense remains cash-funded within margins; the nominal legacy reserve is retained because the actual lease cash schedule is unavailable. The full net gratuity ₹2.9774 crore is already within the separate ₹5.6006 crore year-1 provision settlement and is not charged again. [S1]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The bear assumes Fortira contraction followed by weak growth, other technology stagnation, depressed water margins, slower collections and a ₹35 crore minority purchase funded before the April 2028 deadline. Cumulative new debt ₹57.1873 crore and peak/terminal debt ₹66.8369 crore are far beyond the currently described bank line. The zero residual equity is a total modeled price loss, not a liquidation floor or proof of survival. At the conditional ₹12.75 crore funding ceiling the same operating stress instead requires ₹45.4988 crore hypothetical equity at a discounted issue price. Neither lenders nor subscribers are assumed committed. Government receivable delays, employee attrition and failed product commercialization could worsen these outcomes.

The ₹8.02588 crore receivable impairment is noncash: opening recoverable WC falls from ₹73.2175 to ₹65.19162 crore; year-1 closing WC of ₹86.37712 requires ₹21.1855 crore investment. Impairment is deducted in PAT and added back in CFO, so loss of realizable opening assets affects funding once, not as a second cash expense. Opening provisions and minority distributions are separate cash uses. Positive recent CFO, existing cash and named orders are contrary evidence, but do not establish financing availability. [S1][S4][S10][S11][S12]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
At ₹28.10 and 60.331893 million fully diluted shares, 5×/10× prices require approximately ₹847.66/1695.33 crore equity. At 11× exit EBIT, before debt/cash adjustments, that means ₹77.06/154.12 crore EBIT. At an assumed 15% EBIT margin, required revenue is roughly ₹513.73/1027.47 crore, implying 21.0%/39.0% annual growth from FY26 ₹198.146 crore. A 35% net-WC intensity would require about ₹106.59/286.40 crore incremental operating capital over the opening ₹73.2175 crore, before development/physical investment and minority acquisition. These are transparent reverse requirements, not a funded growth forecast or independently measured market-share opportunity.

The base ends at ₹360.09 crore sales and does not reach 5×. Bull reaches about 6.91× the dated price, not 10×, through 18%/22% technology growth, improved margins, faster cash conversion and successful development commercialization. It still requires temporary new debt and a ₹30 crore minority purchase. The two-way grid also models a lower 9× terminal multiple. The 5× path is arithmetically possible under an aggressive combination, not established as probable; 10× needs more scale, capital or valuation than the completed bull case. [S1][S4][S7][S90]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Require audited Fortira/other component accounts and an acquisition-date cash/net-asset bridge; follow organic sales after eliminations and customer-level collections, especially balances older than three years. Obtain the49% purchase formula and financing plan before treating the base as an expected return. Track development go-live, amortization, actual product revenue and operating cash after capex. Official 60-session data are complete: conservative median ₹19.812 lakh gives ₹5 lakh exit 5.05 days at 5%,12.62 days at 2%,2.52 days at 10%. A 4000-share lot costs ₹112400; four lots ₹449600. REG1 flags fewer than 100 PANs, market-making-period expiry, SME trading caution and price variation, effective 21 October; these justify L4 despite observed daily trading. Named-list nonmatches are not blanket execution clearance. [S1][S7][S90][S91][S92][S93][S94][S96]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Unresolved acquisition-quality hold with commercial upside, not a completed investment recommendation. Supported factors can be compared cautiously, but missing REV and expected-return evidence prevent aggregate ranking. Neither an unaudited-component disclosure alone nor an approved related-party transaction proves misconduct. Conversely, an unmodified group opinion does not resolve recoverability and minority funding. Reassess after component/collection/transaction evidence permits an expected rather than merely conditional return case. [S1][S4][S7][S8]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: FY26/FY25 reports, IPO history, acquisition/listing/loan notices and subsequent orders were actually reviewed. FY24 issuer download remained incomplete after recovery attempts; FY25 audited comparatives supply FY24 history, not a false full-report-read claim. Foreign average/closing currency policy, warrant/preference flows and deposit reclassification were reconciled where supported. Acquisition cash remains diagnostic because opening acquired cash and full purchase accounting were not located. Annual model bridges, funding alternatives, dilution and sensitivity calculations are completed; material evidence holds remain genuine rather than substitutes for unperformed calculations. No external publication performed; exact regulatory passages require review. [S1][S2][S3][S4][S5][S6]

GOV.reason: Approved allocation and transaction disclosure are positive; material unaudited components, audit-trail exception and high pay relative to owners profit constrain confidence.

MOAT.reason: Vendor and client relationships provide ordinary advantages; competing cloud/IT providers, pass-through mix and unverified recurring retention prevent a stronger moat score.

REV.reason: NS because acquisition/FX/intercompany/gross-cloud effects materially obscure a comparable demand basis; reported growth is calculated and not assigned an arbitrary acquisition haircut.

DUR.reason: Named orders and North American access support runway; aged receivables, buyout funding and unproven product commercialization constrain self-funded scaling.

CAP.reason: Full-capital return appears decent, but development-expensing lowers average proxy to 14.64%; acquisition integration and immature software cohorts limit evidence of repeatable incremental superiority.

CASH.reason: Five-year negative cumulative CFO, near-zero latest pre-acquisition FCF and older receivables outweigh two recent positive CFO years; transaction cash classification remains unresolved.

BAL.reason: Current cash and modest opening net debt provide an initial cushion, but the April 2028 minority purchase creates a sizable year-2 funding requirement even in the reference case. New funding and renewal are not committed.

EXEC.reason: Acquisition closure and named orders are observable delivery; modernization-framework launch slippage and incomplete cash realization offset them.

EARN.reason: Owners earnings improve, but acquisition, capitalization, one-time labour cost and dilution complicate recurring per-share quality; no blanket addback of future employee cost.

R.reason: Linked model completed but remaining 49% purchase pricing/component cash access not sufficiently evidenced for an expected reference; conditional scenario return is not scored.

D.reason: The linked unconstrained bear now has zero residual equity after retained rent/deposit claims and needs ₹57.19 crore new debt; constrained funding requires hypothetical equity or fails. D2 reflects a severe permanent-loss path, not an assertion of imminent insolvency.

P.reason: Reported 13.4 PE and attractive conditional base offer possible upside, but expected value and margin of safety are not established while cash/buyout assumptions remain unresolved.

L.reason: 5.05 day historical exit is moderate; 4000 lot, fewer-than 100 PAN and market-making-expiry flags justify a lower implementation score.

ranking_eligibility.reason: Incomplete factors and critical evidence hold; bounds are mathematical missing-data bounds, not valuations or ranking scores.

valuation.formula: Business-line EBITDA less physical depreciation and five-year development amortization gives EBIT. CFO = PAT + DA + noncash impairment − change in recoverable operating WC. Cash deducts full development/physical capex, opening provisions, first-two-year minority distributions and year-2 minority purchase. Opening plus half-year draw interest affects debt/equity needs. Terminal equity = EBIT × multiple − debt + cash, divided by evolving diluted shares. Without common dividends, CAGR = (terminal price / 28.1)^(1/5) − 1. Funding-failure cases have no return. Terminal equity also deducts ₹0.1653 crore retained rent-equalisation/refundable-deposit claims; these are not duplicate current employee payments.
